metadata.name: ww-button
metadata.description: A configurable button element supporting styling, icons, and form submission. Inherits text properties.
features: Custom button background through element styles

properties.name: buttonType
properties.description: Button type: regular or form submit

properties.name: hasLeftIcon
properties.description: Bindable boolean controlling whether the left icon is shown. Use a boolean value or bind it to a variable or formula. The editor creates a child ww-icon in the leftIcon slot when this toggle is enabled or bound, even when the binding currently evaluates to false. Preserve explicit false values and bindings.

properties.name: hasRightIcon
properties.description: Bindable boolean controlling whether the right icon is shown. Use a boolean value or bind it to a variable or formula. The editor creates a child ww-icon in the rightIcon slot when this toggle is enabled or bound, even when the binding currently evaluates to false. Preserve explicit false values and bindings.

states.name: focus
states.description: Matches CSS :focus-within while the Button itself or a descendant has focus. Pointer clicks and keyboard navigation can both give focus.

events.name: focus
events.description: Triggered when the button receives focus

events.name: blur
events.description: Triggered when the button loses focus

events.name: keydown
events.description: Triggered on key down while focused

events.name: keyup
events.description: Triggered on key up while focused

slots.name: leftIcon
slots.description: Child ww-icon element displayed on the left side of the button text when hasLeftIcon resolves to true. Holds a full ww-icon element (its own uid, style and size), NOT an icon-name string. Enabling or binding hasLeftIcon creates this child in the editor, including while a binding evaluates to false. Keep the child when the toggle becomes false or its binding is removed so the configured icon can be reused. Configure the icon by editing this child ww-icon; never write an icon name string into content.default.leftIcon via editElement (it breaks the icon).

slots.name: rightIcon
slots.description: Child ww-icon element displayed on the right side of the button text when hasRightIcon resolves to true. Holds a full ww-icon element (its own uid, style and size), NOT an icon-name string. Enabling or binding hasRightIcon creates this child in the editor, including while a binding evaluates to false. Keep the child when the toggle becomes false or its binding is removed so the configured icon can be reused. Configure the icon by editing this child ww-icon; never write an icon name string into content.default.rightIcon via editElement (it breaks the icon).

specifications: Inherits text properties from ww-text element
The text background content property does not exist. Never set content.backgroundColor; use the element style backgroundColor to style the whole button.
Submit type buttons should be used inside a ww-form-container
For form submission workflows, trigger them on the form container, not the submit button

Classes can style padding, colors, borders, and typography. Button does not read gap (including rowGap and columnGap), justifyContent, alignItems, or flexDirection from classes. Set content.default.textAlign (left, center or right) to align the text and icons horizontally. Set style.default.margin on the child ww-icon using the desired spacing as the right margin of a left icon or the left margin of a right icon. Use a layout-capable element such as ww-div for reusable flex or grid layout among children.
Never forget the 'text' prop in the contents. The button will not display without it!
